Model Conversation Relay

A relay keeps two voices distinct while making their exchange traceable. The request remains the caller's exact contribution; the response remains the other model's observed contribution. Carry each across the boundary with its origin intact, so the caller can judge what the answer means for the task. Transport establishes that this response belongs to this request at this conversation; interpretation and acceptance remain further judgments.

Own one exact request/response exchange: exact exchange identity, ordered-turn reconciliation, response-turn completeness, wait/retry decisions, and at most one mutation attempt in flight. Native task/thread and an allowed currently selected controlled Browser carrier are conditional per-operation adapters. Mutation and observation adapters may differ; an observation adapter never submits or resends. Adapters return physical or native observations. The relay decides whether an observable response turn is complete enough to bind; this transport claim says nothing about semantic adequacy, agreement, evidence sufficiency, correctness, or task completion. The caller supplies its exact target binding and retains authority for outbound messages. Reuse actual authorization for this exchange; installing or testing this package does not authorize a submission. Read the installed browser-relay entrypoint completely when selecting its controlled Browser route. It is a conditional companion, available from the same public collection; native-only operations do not need it. See configuration and dependencies.

An installed host-specific provenance owner, such as cloud-local-workflow, may retain surrounding task evidence. It is optional, is not distributed in this collection, and is never required to use this relay. Without it, the caller's existing task records retain that provenance and first-request reconciliation.

Freeze the ready exchange

This relay never creates or selects a destination. Before outbound mutation, require and freeze:

  • exchange_id;
  • exact conversation identity plus caller-supplied target mode and readiness evidence;
  • exact request bytes and SHA-256;
  • latest observed remote turn boundary or explicit absence boundary; and
  • the current operation constraint, if any.

A caller may attach task_id, chat_creation_id, Project-instruction identity, checkpoint identity, title, model-selection evidence, and other provenance to the receipt, but the generic relay entrypoint does not require an enclosing lifecycle's fields. Reject an unready, missing, guessed, substituted, or mode-ambiguous target; mutable or digest-mismatched request; or destination discovery. A title, URL without retained binding, or former Project membership is not target identity. The relay does not separately parse or require User Source, accepted Scheme, artifact, checkpoint purpose, question, local evidence, or authority fields. Those remain with the caller and are represented to relay only by exact target/readiness evidence, request bytes, and optional receipt annotations. Any creation/first-request operation performed before a conversation ID exists is outside this relay and must never be passed here as a guessed or pending target.

Immutable transport evidence

Resolve a task-owned private storage location from the consumer before writing. Keep requests, responses, receipts, account bindings and continuation notes outside public packages, plugin caches and public repositories. Store only the evidence needed for this exchange under the actual data and retention authority. This package supplies no personal account, conversation, profile or storage binding.

Before any mutation, write the exact frozen request to an immutable file and verify its SHA-256. The caller retains any relevant task, creation, Project, model-selection and source/object provenance around the exchange; the generic relay does not parse or duplicate those fields.

After one exact response is bound, write one immutable JSON receipt containing exchange ID, conversation identity and target-mode evidence, request and response paths/digests, remote user/assistant turn identities, operation-adapter evidence, acknowledgement/in-flight reconciliation evidence, and Browser cleanup or release evidence when applicable. Verify and return the receipt path and SHA-256. The caller binds that receipt through its existing task handoff. No second transport ledger is required.

ChatGPT operation adapters

For each observation or mutation operation, select the smallest currently capable adapter that can address the frozen exact target and return evidence required for that operation. Native task/thread and controlled Browser are both eligible when their current exact-target evidence and owner constraints permit the operation. Select the carrier from current host policy, actual capabilities, and the operation's needs while retaining the frozen target binding. Neither origin permits creation, target substitution, URL synthesis, or selection by title, recency, similarity, or former Project membership. Browser never bypasses a missing native authorization or tool boundary.

For an exact ChatGPT advisory conversation, use a native codex_app adapter when the current host actually exposes that callable tool and its exact target binding is available. Inspect the currently callable schema and its target semantics first. For example, a host exposing this binding through functions.exec can read it with:

const observed = await tools.mcp__codex_app__read_thread({
  threadId: exact_conversation_id,
  turnLimit: 20,
});

Use tools.mcp__codex_app__send_message_to_thread only for a selected, actually authorized mutation operation and only with that exact threadId. Its current schema and authorization contract govern whether and how that operation is allowed; a readable native target does not establish send authority. Resolve deferred tools through the current host's supported discovery. A name in this example does not establish availability. Use integrations supported and authorized by the recipient’s current host; do not infer a usable adapter from a tool name. If the native operation is unavailable, use an already permitted controlled carrier or report that operation's concrete capability limit. For a Browser operation, follow the selected controlled carrier's owning instructions and pass exact destination, operation (observe or submit), frozen payload for submit, prior boundary, and lifecycle requirement. Read and use browser-relay only when that is the selected carrier. Browser returns physical observations and cleanup evidence only. The relay decides semantic turn binding, completion, waiting, and retry. Never persist a current task's transient browser/provider ID as general Skill policy.

Host confirmation, login, credential, consent, and human-action boundaries remain with runtime owners. Creating a new conversation, changing its model, or changing account settings is outside this relay primitive.

First submission and interrupted continuation

Conversation creation and a first request sent by another owner precede this relay. Require its retained exact conversation binding, frozen request and last known attempt evidence. Reconcile that first submission before any follow-up or retry: if accepted, recover its matching user turn and response or continue waiting; if acceptance is uncertain, retain that uncertainty without sending again. Never recreate a conversation or repeat a first request to discover what happened.

After interruption, restore the same exchange ID, request bytes and digest, exact target, prior ordered-turn boundary, acknowledgement and resend history, last observation, and pending wait decision from the caller's continuity. Observe the same target before the next mutation. Missing evidence is an unresolved boundary, not permission to reset attempt counts, adopt a nearby conversation or assume the request was never sent. Native and Browser observation can reconcile each other only when both establish that same target and ordered exchange.

One exact conversation exchange

  1. Verify the request digest immediately before a mutation attempt and reconcile the latest ordered turn through any capable observation adapter. If the request may already exist, bind its latest attempt before deciding whether to wait or retry.
  2. Retain each operation-adapter identity in transport_evidence. Observation never submits or resends. Before another mutation after any adapter may have changed the target, reconcile ordered turns again.
  3. If the target reports running or paused, use the discrete waiting policy below before observing again. Otherwise submit exact frozen bytes without translation, normalization, summarization, wrapping, or explanation. Keep at most one mutation attempt in flight.
  4. Any successful return from the selected mutation operation counts as submission acknowledgement, even when it contains only target identity and no remote turn identity, unless the adapter explicitly reports non-acceptance or error. After acknowledgement, keep that attempt in flight until the matching request/response turn becomes observable or the adapter supplies explicit evidence that no submission was accepted. An idle target or temporarily absent matching turn is observation lag, not resend eligibility. If acknowledgement cannot be reconciled, return the uncertain transport boundary rather than resend.
  5. A same-target exact resend is eligible only after explicit non-acceptance evidence or after an observable matching request turn is followed, after reconciliation, by a terminal or idle non-running target with no complete assistant response, including a missing, interrupted, or truncated response. Permit at most one exact resend for that observable terminal-response boundary. Preserve exchange, target, chat_creation_id, and request digest. Identity, authentication, challenge, consent, safety, ownership, digest, or cleanup failure stops without substitution.
  6. Retain the exact response and evidence in the same calling-model turn, write and verify the immutable receipt defined above, and return its path and digest. Browser cleanup or release readback belongs in cleanup_evidence.

Discrete waiting for Web generation

After submission reconciliation establishes an accepted request still generating, choose when to check again from the observed progress, elapsed time, expected remaining work, and the cost of noticing completion later. Estimate when another observation is likely to be useful, balancing response latency against local model usage. Reassess after each due observation: evidence of nearing completion can justify a shorter wait; substantial remaining work or little change can justify a longer one. Do not prescribe a fixed interval, initial sequence, or backoff ladder. Treat unavailable progress as uncertainty, not an invented percentage or a reason for rapid polling. This applies to advisory heavy work and Web behavior evaluations after Prompt or Skill edits alike. Initial submission reconciliation and an explicit user request to inspect now are separate from routine generation checks; an actual completion or error event can be handled when delivered.

Between checks, let the host's supported passive wait or deferred wake-up carry the time, or continue independent useful work. Preserve the exact conversation, request/turn binding, last observation and its time, progress estimate with its uncertainty, and chosen next check time with a brief reason before yielding. Use existing task continuity or a small task-owned temporary note; update it after each check rather than creating a separate durable ledger. This note retains the waiting decision but does not itself schedule execution. Use the host's current scheduling and continuation contract; verify any scheduled wake-up before relying on it. A short tool timeout does not make another conversation read due. Avoid repeated screenshots, thread reads, refreshes, short model/tool polling loops, or ongoing reasoning merely to occupy the interval. Do not introduce a custom watcher or daemon. If no supported continuation can carry the wait, report that concrete limitation and retained pending exchange rather than pretending a future check is scheduled.

At the due check, read the smallest evidence needed to distinguish running, complete, and actionable failure. While still running, retain the same request and choose the next useful check from the new evidence; elapsed time alone never justifies resubmission, restart, or a duplicate evaluation. On completion, consume and bind the response; on an actionable failure, follow the existing reconciliation and retry boundary. Retire any task-owned wake-up when its exchange is complete or cancelled.

Result package

exchange_id
target_identity
target_mode_evidence
request_path
request_sha256
response_path
remote_user_turn_id
remote_assistant_turn_id
remote_assistant_text
remote_assistant_sha256

cleanup_evidence
receipt_path
receipt_sha256

The calling model decides whether to persist, evaluate, forward, or reject the answer. The relay records a bound response turn and does not create a semantic-success scalar or a correctness/completion result.

An optional installed host-specific provenance owner can add task, attributable user source, candidate/Plan, result, Project-instruction, model-selection and advice provenance around one exchange; otherwise the caller retains these in its existing task records. Preserve strongest evidence and exact missing proof. Do not choose a semantic follow-up, create a conversation, rewrite either side, start another model, add a coordinator, registry, state machine, queue, daemon, watcher, retry database, or new Browser runtime.
